headline: NASA picks lunar successor. FCC auctions spectrum. Sphinx wins big.
deck: This week sees significant moves in lunar missions, spectrum auctions, and defense contracts.

stories.head: Advanced Space wins lunar mission follow-up contract
stories.body: NASA has selected Advanced Space to succeed the CAPSTONE lunar mission with a new small satellite designed for rendezvous technology testing. This contract underscores the moon's continued appeal as a testing ground for advanced space operations. Financial details remain undisclosed, but expect a hefty investment as lunar ambitions grow.
stories.soWhat: If the moon is the new frontier for testing, expect more players to jump into lunar missions, possibly diluting the market for contracts.

stories.head: FCC's upper C-band auction could net $6 billion
stories.body: The upcoming FCC auction for upper C-band spectrum is projected to generate over $6 billion for satellite operators, highlighting the value of clearing spectrum in the GEO sector. This auction is seen as a critical opportunity for companies looking to enhance their communication capabilities, particularly as demand for satellite services continues to rise.
stories.soWhat: With spectrum becoming the new gold rush, companies without a strong spectrum strategy may soon find themselves at a competitive disadvantage.

stories.head: Sphinx Defense lands $287 million software contract
stories.body: Sphinx Defense has secured a $287 million contract to develop mission planning software for next-gen strategic satellites. This contract emphasizes the increasing importance of software in enhancing satellite capabilities and operational efficiency. As the defense sector invests heavily in software upgrades, this could be a bellwether for future contracts.
stories.soWhat: If software is the backbone of modern defense, companies that can deliver robust solutions will continue to thrive, leaving hardware-focused firms in the dust.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's growth
watchlist.body: With a recent $190 million Series C, True Anomaly is poised to capitalize on increasing demand for co-orbital security solutions.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves closer to launch
watchlist.body: Having passed its critical design review, the Dream Chaser DoD variant is now one step closer to operational deployment, which could shake up logistics for defense missions.

watchlist.title: Watch for FCC auction outcomes
watchlist.body: The results of the upcoming upper C-band auction could reshape the competitive landscape in satellite communications, affecting stock prices and partnerships.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program, Palantir's continued involvement in defense tech indicates a solidified role in future military operations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
